info.name: The Discount Window — machine surface
info.description: The read-only JSON surface of the Discount Window, matching docs/openapi.yaml. Import this collection, run the server (`npm start`), and read the book the way an agent would: no screen-scraping, no secrets, and no way to move money from here — that is the point. The desk-only routes use basic auth with username `desk`; on a public demo, use the password the README names.

variable.description: Any id from 'The book'. The seeded ids contain the hash of the seed, so copy a live one; the four worked examples are A-1042, A-1043, A-1043-R2 and A-1054, with A-1043 and A-1054 refused.
Basic auth for desk:thesharedpassword — replace with the deployed demo's password. On localhost with no password configured, the desk needs no header at all.

request.description: Open to everyone: the audit chain re-walked on every call. If ok is false, the book has been tampered with and says so.
Aggregate vitals with no login: chain integrity, book counts, ledger balances, webhook summary.
Every invoice with score, band, price and status. Add ?status=REFUSED for the refusal archive as data.

Copy an id from 'The book'. Returns the eleven checks, the score, the price, the slices, the audit chain and the extraction — the whole deal room as an object. Refusals serve the same fix sentence a seller sees.
Double-entry postings by transaction, account totals, and the last twenty webhooks PayPal delivered — with their signature verdicts.

No basic auth on this route — its authority is PayPal's signature check. Without a configured webhook id the check cannot run, so the honest answer is 503 'signature verification unavailable; retry' and nothing is stored. With a webhook id configured and PayPal answering that the signature is bad, the answer is 200 'unverified, stored' and it changes nothing.
